title: Stochastic stability of master--slave synchronization for a class of PDEs with Burgers-type nonlinearity
summary: We investigate the stochastic stability of master--slave synchronization for a class of nonlinear evolution equations sharing a Burgers-type convective nonlinearity and a polynomial linear differential operator, including the Burgers, Kuramoto--Sivashinsky, Kawahara, Benney--Lin, and Nikolaevskiy equations. Under periodic boundary conditions, each equation is represented through a Fourier truncation of order $K$, yielding a real state of one-sided complex Fourier coefficients, which is coupled to a slave system driven by observed master data.
